cross_response_observations: Several common defect patterns emerge across the eight responses. First, a pervasive misconception about periodicity appears: both Response A and Response G incorrectly claim a period-2 (alternating P/N) pattern, asserting that 'all even positions are P and all odd positions are N' or invoking Nim XOR to justify alternation. The actual game has period 3 for P-positions (0, 3, 6, 9, ...). Second, move set errors are prevalent: Response B excludes 1 (2^0) from the move set, while Response F bizarrely expands it to include all integers 1-100 by misinterpreting 'powers of two' as 'all numbers formable by summing powers of two.' Third, base case errors affect Responses C and D, both incorrectly setting position 0 to N instead of P, though they provide different rationales. Fourth, framework confusion is evident: Response E uses Sprague-Grundy mex computation unnecessarily, while Response G misapplies Nim XOR to a single-pile subtraction game. Fifth, computational failures appear in Response D and E (truncated strings) and Response H (infinite looping on base case). Sixth, heuristic pattern-matching without DP verification occurs in Responses A and G, where the period-2 claim is asserted without computing the actual recurrence. Notably, no response is fully correct, and none of the eight models successfully computed the correct 101-character P/N classification string. The most fundamental errors are the move set misdefinition in B and F, which are upstream of any arithmetic issues.
